modes.productCapability: One managed Offline-authorized device per tenant branch, one shared encrypted branch namespace, continuous Offline reads and durable command creation, and PIN switching for employees enrolled Online on the exact account/tenant/branch/device namespace.
modes.authorityLifetime: Event-driven validity with no time-based Offline employee, read, or command disablement. Old synchronization age is visibility and risk evidence only.
modes.connectivity: Required for initial enrollment/bootstrap and used opportunistically thereafter for revalidation and synchronization; not a periodic operating prerequisite.
modes.securityLevel: Human-accepted managed-PWA residual-risk model. Device-bound encryption is independent of employee PIN selection; no hardware, trusted-clock, or tamper-proof-counter guarantee.
modes.implementationEffort: High: verified Online account bootstrap, device authority, structured employee selector enrollment, device-bound protected local state, durable command pipeline, Core employee/device binding, inventory frontier, eight-payment parity, effect ledger, security review, and qualification.
modes.operationalBurden: Dedicated managed OS account/device, full-disk encryption, screen lock, kiosk browser, restricted DevTools/profile/software, Online enrollment/removal administration, warnings and synchronization monitoring, incident/loss process.
residualRisk: Compromised same-origin code may invoke non-extractable WebCrypto keys.
Browser-local attempt counters and clocks are not tamper-proof.
An unlocked or privileged compromised device is outside the Mode A guarantee.
Remote employee, permission, PIN-generation, branch, or device revocation is not discovered during a long outage until trusted reconnect.
modes.supportsAllAuthorizedEmployeesAfterResta: All previously enrolled employees whose exact namespace package and protected state remain valid; newly authorized or never-enrolled employees require Online enrollment.
modes.permitsDurableOfflineCommands: Design intent yes, but implementation remains blocked by the enumerated server/Core/inventory/effect/security prerequisites.

modes.productCapability: Native Keychain/Keystore and platform protections may harden the same continuous Offline model where capabilities are proven.
modes.securityLevel: Potentially stronger device custody, but capability is device/platform dependent and not assumed universally.
modes.implementationEffort: Very high native platform work in addition to Mode A server/Core prerequisites.
modes.operationalBurden: Supported-device matrix, app signing, MDM, platform attestation and replacement processes.
modes.supportsAllAuthorizedEmployeesAfterResta: If enrolled and platform policy passes.
modes.permitsDurableOfflineCommands: Only after the same missing server/Core prerequisites.

modes.reason: Does not support multiple enrolled employees switching Offline on the shared branch device.
Creates a connectivity prerequisite and does not support continuous Offline restart, reboot, or employee switching.

selectedValidityEvents: trusted reconnect discovers server revocation, deactivation, permission change, PIN generation change, branch transfer, or device replacement
authorized local employee removal or governed local administrative lock
namespace, schema, signature, key, binding, integrity, or protected-state validation failure
registered device identity or account/tenant/branch binding mismatch
nonBlockingFacts: temporary Online Auth token expiry during an outage while explicit logout has not occurred
decisionRules: Mode A is selected as a product/security decision, not implemented by documentation.
No hidden absolute, sliding, grace, or periodic-connectivity expiry may disable otherwise valid Offline employee/read/command authority.
Primary Auth alone never unlocks sensitive data or supplies the acting employee.
Explicit establishment logout disables Offline PIN entry and requires same-account Online authentication before recovery.
Restart without explicit logout requires employee PIN selection again but does not require Internet.
Employee PIN never derives, wraps or unwraps the business-data DEK.
Trusted reconnect revalidates before synchronization or new server acquisition.
Mode B remains optional future hardening; Modes C and D remain rejected.
